slides.texte_overlay:
psychology facts that will
change how you see people

the halo effect

people assume someone good at one thing is good at everything. knowing this helps you judge people more fairly, and see past quick, shallow first impressions.

the reciprocity rule

when someone does something kind for us, we feel a strong urge to return it. small generous acts create far more lasting goodwill than you would ever expect.

the mere exposure effect

people tend to like things simply because they've seen them often. it's why familiar faces feel friendlier, and why showing up consistently matters so very much.

the curiosity effect

curious people are seen as warmer and more likeable. 5 minutes a day learning something new, like a planet or a painting, makes curiosity a natural habit.

the spotlight effect

people notice your mistakes far less than you think. everyone is busy worrying about their own spotlight, so please give yourself a whole lot more grace.
